object_types.name: Patient
object_types.definition: A person who books and attends medical appointments at the clinic

source_references.excerpt: Patients book appointments... Patients have a patient ID -- it's on their card.

object_types.name: Doctor
object_types.definition: A medical practitioner who conducts patient appointments

source_references.excerpt: Doctors have a license number.

object_types.name: Appointment

object_types.name: AppointmentStatus
object_types.definition: The current status of an appointment, restricted to one of four allowed values

source_references.excerpt: Every appointment also has a status. The status is one of: scheduled, checked-in, completed, or cancelled... An appointment always has exactly one status from that list.

ambiguities.description: Appointment scheduling uniqueness across date/time/doctor: The transcript states appointments are booked on a specific date and at a specific time slot, but does not explicitly clarify whether the same doctor can have multiple appointments at the same time slot, or whether a given date/time slot can accommodate only one patient per doctor. This affects whether appointments need a composite uniqueness constraint spanning Doctor, AppointmentDate, and TimeSlot.

source_references.excerpt: Every appointment is on a date and at a time slot -- we book in fixed slots like 09:00 or 09:30.

ambiguities.description: ExamRoom usage: The transcript introduces ExamRoom as a concept with a room number but does not clarify whether appointments are assigned to specific exam rooms, whether a room can hold multiple appointments simultaneously, or whether rooms are optional for appointments. It is unclear if a relationship between Appointment and ExamRoom should be modeled.

source_references.excerpt: Exam rooms have a room number.

ambiguities.description: VisitReason optionality: The transcript states 'An appointment can have a visit reason' but does not clarify the reverse -- whether a given visit reason must be associated with at least one appointment (mandatory on the VisitReason side). The model assumes visit reasons are optional inputs with no requirement to be reused.

source_references.excerpt: An appointment can have a visit reason the patient gives when booking

ambiguities.description: Specialty uniqueness: The transcript states 'Every doctor has exactly one specialty' but does not clarify whether multiple doctors can share the same specialty (i.e., whether Specialty is a closed list or allows many-to-one mapping). This affects whether Specialty should be modeled as a value type or a distinct entity type with its own identifier.

source_references.excerpt: Every doctor has exactly one specialty, like cardiology or general practice.

ambiguities.description: AppointmentStatus constraint placement: AppointmentStatus is modeled as a value type with an intrinsic value_constraint listing the allowed values. However, it is possible the constraint is contextual to a specific role or fact type rather than a universal restriction on the AppointmentStatus value type itself. This is a minor semantic question but does not affect the functional model.

source_references.excerpt: Every appointment also has a status. The status is one of: scheduled, checked-in, completed, or cancelled.

ambiguities.description: Primary doctor vs. appointment doctor relationship: The transcript explicitly states that a patient's primary doctor is 'separate from who they happen to see in a given appointment', confirming that 'Patient has primary Doctor' and 'Appointment is with Doctor' are distinct relationships. However, there is no explicit constraint stated regarding whether the appointment doctor must, should, or cannot be the same as the primary doctor. This may warrant a business rule clarification.

source_references.excerpt: Yes, every patient has exactly one primary doctor. That's separate from who they happen to see in a given appointment.
